event_description: Montana Trails is looking forward to opening our doors for the first summer artwalk of the 2018 season in downtown Bozeman with a great collection of historic and contemporary art. The Bozeman artwalk is from 6 - 8 PM. Montana Trails is proud to carry a large variety of western art, including landscape, wildlife, figurative, and still life works with a range of styles from impressionist to traditional American in both painting and sculpture. We represent a variety of contemporary and period artists. Among our collection, you will find legendary period artists such as Nicolai Fechin and Ace Powell, as well as sought after contemporaries like Tom Gilleon and Nicholas Coleman. Since 1990, Steve Zabel and the crew at Montana Trails Gallery have provided personal attention for both beginning and seasoned collectors. Montana Trails specializes in finding, buying, selling, and building collections of quality American paintings and sculptures, from the early 1800's to present. We attend major art auctions and provide information, appraisal, bidding, and curatorial services.

event_name: 2020 Solo Exhibition featuring DAVID FREDERICK RILEY
event_description: You and a guest are invited to the preview party with David Frederick Riley on Wednesday, August 12th, Thursday, August 13th, and Friday August 14th from 5pm - 7pm. Due to the current guidelines, we are having three preview parties to allow adaquate social distancing. We want everyone to have the opportunity to preview the show and stay safe at the same time. We look forward to seeing you there! Please RSVP at info@montanatrails.com, or (406) 586 - 2166. David Riley is a gallery artist, portrait and wildlife painter, and illustrator. His painting is inspired by the universal narratives of the human condition, emotion and the similar elements that appear in Nature. David works primarily in oil, contrasting contemporary color fields and abstract space with traditional handling of the human form. He uses color harmonies to showcase emotion and the vibrancy of life. His work frequently illustrates themes of emotional and spiritual growth. David’s southwestern contemporary works are a unique approach to the wildlife and persons of the West: bison, longhorns, bears and iconic Native American figures. His palette is usually monochromatic, but the power of the imagery creates such an impression, that color is not missed. He has just commenced a collection of cowboys.

event_description: You and a guest are invited to the preview party with Dan Metz on Wednesday, September 23rd & Thursday, September 24th, from 5pm - 7pm. Due to the current guidelines, we are having two preview parties to allow adaquate social distancing. We want everyone to have the opportunity to preview the show and stay safe at the same time. We look forward to seeing you there! Please RSVP at info@montanatrails.com, or (406) 586 - 2166. The mountains of the American west have been a magnet for Dan Metz from his first remembrance. Since 1974, from the Gates of the Arctic to the Wrangells, the St. Elias and down the Rockies through Wyoming he has gone ‘in country’ to his subjects where they live. Only in this way can he hope to imbue his work with the intrinsic nature and spirit of the themes he loves to portray. The scope of his fieldwork is an anomaly these days and it is evident. He has been there. There is only one goal – to make better paintings. His quest is not for some cold, mathematical precision but for a greater truth – the living, breathing essence of the animal. Beginning as an illustrator in 1973, Dan knows how to “make a picture”. Fine draftsmanship and design, along with a thorough knowledge of his subjects, are the hallmarks of his work.

event_description: Montana Trails Gallery anticipates a new collection of paintings and sculptures for a One Man Exhibition with Joe Wayne. Joe Wayne was born in Whitefish Montana and now resides in Livingston. Several years ago Wayne came to the Bozeman–Livingston area where he began working in local bronze foundries and studying art. Out of college Wayne went directly into production as a welder, metalworker, and patina artist. Preferring to work from nature, whether it’s a model, still life, or landscape and to capture the individual personality of the subject is of most importance. "The excitement of aesthetic and impressionistic expression carries over to the studio and what fuels my desire to paint and sculpt is the continuing inspiration from masters who have accomplished the traditions of art." In coordination with Downtown Bozeman Artwalk 6-8pm

event_description: The A. Banks team is excited to welcome back Aaron Hazel for a solo exhibition during our grand opening party! This esteemed painter who focuses on working mostly with a palate knife will be back on August 9th, for his third show with the gallery. Swing by A. event_description: Come by A. Banks Gallery on July 11th for an art walk you won't forget! Montana painter, Cecilee Schulz will be here for a live demonstration into her unique and unmissable process. Cecilee, daughter and student of renowned artist Troy Collins, has long had her hands in the painting scene. Quite literally in fact, many of Collins’s originals have her hidden fingerprints, which she insisted were a lucky selling omen. Painting in the studio with her “Pops” started as early as 2006, but over the last few years has turned it into a fiery passion of her own. While continuing to study under her dad, and family friend Robert Moore, she is developing a style that represents her own expression, authenticity, and love of color. The Bitterroot Valley is where the creating happens in a shared space with her dad. The sovereign view sets the stage for collaboration and vision to ignite.

event_description: Join us for the opening of Knox Kronenberg's first solo show at MTG on July 18th from 6pm - 8pm. event_description: Join us from 6pm - 8pm on Friday, August 8th for a solo exhibition featuring Meagan Blessing. “Illuminations” celebrates hidden moments of brilliance nestled within the ordinary rhythms of the natural world. Light draws us to itself. Every living thing has an innate compass guiding it toward the vibrant cadence of existence.This body of work explores the intersections between what we see with our eyes and what we sense in our hearts. I use vivid color and bold brushstrokes that form interlocking shapes to create mosaic-like portraits that, while representational, often bleed over the line into abstraction.In my world, the mundane often mingles with the fantastic. Nature is like the threads of a sacred tapestry woven into the very fabric of life, and it is in the embrace of the great outdoors that we frequently find sanctuary. We are, all of us, instinctively aware that the wild whispers secrets to the soul. Each painting in this collection depicts an intangible facet of our lives, such as joy, hope, epiphany, or reflection. Not every question is answered, and not every image is fully formed. The human experience is rich and varied, and often, it’s easier to glimpse our true selves from an outside perspective. It is my intention to create art that is both uplifting and compelling, inviting viewers to pause, reflect, and recognize pieces.

event_description: I was asked to write a little bit about the show. These sort of requests always make me pause for a moment because I have learned that my purest form of communication is through the visual spectrum. What am I trying to say through my work? What is the meaning behind the pieces? Good question. Painting is a strange form of expression because the meaning behind the blobs of paint can change from viewer to viewer. This concept is well understood by anyone who has spent any amount of time enjoying or experiencing art. I guess I view my job as the interpreter of my mind. I have a firm belief that our concisenesses are all connected and that bits and pieces of the human experience are universal. I like things that we can all understand. That feeling when you fall down and scrape your knee, that pang of discomfort in the stomach when you have gone too long without eating, the sound of a baby cooing. Most of the paintings completed for this show focus on human connection and my desire to share expression without the use of language. The work is a chance to connect with me and anyone around you. Every eyeball letting in light and every gut feeling adds one more fiber to the web that weaves us all together. – Cyrus Walker
